questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given an Angle
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070169/assets/bb15327593f4452d177ac7d6fbd910c765c847874505b35a13bdd69b123242d0.png)

Find the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={45}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({45}^{∘}) & =\frac{x+3}{2x} \\ 1 & =\frac{x+3}{2x} \\ 2x & =x+3 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =x+3=3+3=6, \\ AB & =2x=2(3)=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 6 \\  & =18.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Area of a Triangle by Solving for a Variable Given a Trigonometric Ratio of One Angle
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070169/assets/6d32c4a97154570f8a66f89ba5fee46f11aa09d2cd152edb4aa05f2613d035f3.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{3}{2},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\frac{3}{2}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \frac{3}{2} & =\frac{x+3}{3x-5} \\ 3(3x-5) & =2(x+3) \\ 9x-15 & =2x+6 \\ 7x & =21 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =3x-5=3(3)-5=4, \\ AC & =x+3=3+3=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 4 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070169/assets/7e555f1574ba37c5b2ac8f4bca54f0d9e2b449e1351f792feba334ddbdc5b8df.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\sqrt{3},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\sqrt{3}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \sqrt{3} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}(x-4)}{8-x} \\ \sqrt{3}(8-x) & =\sqrt{3}(x-4) \\ 8-x & =x-4 \\ 2x & =12 \\ x & =6\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =8-x=8-6=2, \\ AC & =\sqrt{3}(x-4)=\sqrt{3}(6-4)=2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2\sqrt{3} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Area of a Triangle Given a Trigonometric Ratio of an Angle and the Length of a Leg
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070169/assets/58af9726d81e1d926f814736fa92dc95c427d4346c40252470380f51a5fcf50a.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =3,$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta =3,$ where $\theta =m∠B.$ Notice we're also given the length of the side $\overset{―}{AC}$ opposite to $∠B.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to find the length of the adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ 3 & =\frac{15}{BC} \\ BC & =\frac{15}{3} \\ BC & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 15\cdot 5 \\  & =37.5.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070169/assets/d792a93992bbd915063156e0c8fb4f65a71f1609cee5141609e4a5ca6ba6f405.png)

The **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
questions.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠C={30}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠C,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AB}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠C) & =\frac{AB}{BC} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({30}^{∘}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}(x-1)}{2x+1} \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}(x-1)}{2x+1} \\ \sqrt{3}(2x+1) & =3\sqrt{3}(x-1) \\ 2x+1 & =3x-3 \\ x & =4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\sqrt{3}(x-1)=\sqrt{3}(4-1)=3\sqrt{3}, \\ BC & =2x+1=2(4)+1=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\sqrt{3}\cdot 9 \\  & =\frac{27\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
